newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour MP says he was threatened with expulsion.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour MP says he was threatened with expulsion.

text.p: A member of Britain's ruling Labour Party said on Tuesday he had been threatened with expulsion if he opposed the government in a referendum to set up an elected assembly in Wales.

Veteran MP Llew Smith, who represents the Welsh seat of Blaenau Gwent in the British parliament, said Welsh Secretary Ron Davies had told him he would be ejected from the parliamentary Labour party if he campaigned against a Welsh assembly later this year.

In the manifesto that helped it win a landslide voctory in Britain's May 1 general election, Labour included a pledge to hold a referendum on setting up a Welsh assembly as part of plans for devolution there and in Scotland.
Smith, who opposes Welsh devolution, said he had discussed the matter with Davies.

"I had a meeting with Ron Davies -- two meetings in fact -- and he informed me that if I should campaign against a Welsh assembly I'd be kicked out of the parliamentary Labour Party," Smith said on BBC radio.

He added: "In all the years I've been in the Labour Party -- often involving controversial issues -- I've never experienced the kind of threats and intolerance which I have over the past number of months."
Both before and after the election, Labour has been at pains to maintain discipline and avoid the bitter in-fighting that cost the Conservative Party dearly.
Smith's allegations represent probably the most vehement public denunciation of party control from within the ranks since Labour won the election.
Davies, however, denied he had threatened Smith.
"There is no question of threats or intimidation, as has been alleged," he said on the same radio programme.
Although the two men had discussed the possible consequences of Smith's course of action, Smith knew that Davies did not have the authority to expel him from the party, the Welsh secretary said.
But he made clear that he expected Smith and other MPs to show loyalty to Labour's policies, whatever their personal feelings.
"I expected individual MPs, whatever their personal feelings, would show a degree of loyalty to the party which allowed them to be elected MPs," Davies said.
"If they failed to do so, we would have to look at the action which would be available to the parliamentary Labour Party."
He added: "It's one thing to be tolerant of strongly held views.

"It's quite another matter if individuals wish to flout the election manifesto on which they were elected, to show disloyalty to their government, which they were elected to support and to campaign publicly against the Labour Party, allying themselves with the Conservative Party in a public referendum."
